frontier_question: Why did the United States move to force TikTok's sale or ban it between 2024 and 2025, and how was the dispute resolved?

chunks.content: The Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act — signed by President Biden on 2024-04-24 — required ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90), or face a US ban. The Supreme Court upheld the law 9-0 (per curiam) on 2025-01-17, one day before the effective date of 2025-01-19. TikTok went dark in the US on 2025-01-18/19 (roughly 14 hours) and was restored 2025-01-19 after President Trump pledged to pause enforcement; his executive order of 2025-01-20 delayed enforcement for 75 days. The resolution was an Oracle-led deal (announced 2025-06-10 per Bloomberg) giving Oracle about a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations, with SoftBank and other investors participating; Vice President JD Vance led the White House negotiations, and ByteDance retained a majority interest. The national-security case rested on Chinese government access to US user data and the algorithm (CFIUS review, Project Texas hosting). The app stayed live, structured as a joint venture rather than an outright sale — "Project Texas": US user data in Oracle's cloud under US control — with the final ownership structure completed through 2025.

prior_gap_texts: The United States moved to force TikTok's sale or ban it primarily due national-security concerns regarding potential Chinese government access to US user data and the platform's algorithm, as determined during CFIUS review [Source: ev-1].

This concern led President Biden to sign the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act on 2024-04-24, which mandated that ByteDance divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90) or face a ban in the US [Source: ev-1].
The dispute was resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on 2025-06-10, rather than an outright sale [Source: ev-1].

Under this agreement, Oracle received approximately a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations, with participation from SoftBank and other investors, while ByteDance retained a majority interest [Source: ev-1].
The resolution involved structuring the app as a joint venture under "Project Texas," which kept US user data hosted in Oracle's cloud under US control to address security risks [Source: ev-1].

This process occurred after the Supreme Court upheld the law 9-0 on 2025-17 (per curiam), just before the effective date of 2025-2025; following a brief period where TikTok went dark for roughly 14 hours on 2025/2025, President Trump pledged to pause enforcement and issued an executive order on 20-20 that delayed enforcement for 75 days while final ownership structures were completed through 2025 [Source: ev-1].
